fields.title: Obicetrapib approved to lower LDL-cholesterol in adults with primary hypercholesterolaemia and/or mixed dyslipidaemia

main_text:
Obicetrapib approved to lower LDL-cholesterol in adults with primary hypercholesterolaemia and/or mixed dyslipidaemia
Obicetrapib blocks the transfer of cholesteryl esters from HDL (‘good’ cholesterol) to other lipoproteins, helping to lower LDL (‘bad’) cholesterol. It is licenced to be taken on its own, or in combination with a patient’s existing cholesterol lowering therapies, and is only available on prescription, as a film-coated tablet to be taken once daily by mouth.
Julian Beach, MHRA Executive Director, Operations, said:
Primary hypercholesterolaemia and mixed dyslipidaemia cause high levels of blood cholesterol. We are pleased to be able to authorise a new treatment option to help people with these conditions lower their cholesterol. As with all products, we will keep the safety of obicetrapib under close review.
The benefit of obicetrapib was demonstrated in two 52-week, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled studies involving adults with primary hypercholesterolaemia and/or mixed dyslipidaemia. In the two studies, obicetrapib reduced LDL-C by 36% and 33% respectively, compared with placebo. The maximum effect of obicetrapib in reducing LDL-C was seen as early as week four and was maintained throughout the one-year treatment period in both studies.
The most common side effects with obicetrapib (which may affect up to 1 in 10 people) are dizziness; headache; high blood pressure (hypertension); abdominal pain; diarrhoea; increased blood levels of glucose; and increased blood levels of creatine phosphokinase (an enzyme released into the blood when muscle is damaged). Anyone who suspects they are having a side effect from this medicine are encouraged to talk to their doctor, pharmacist or nurse and report it directly to the Yellow Card scheme.
Notes to editors
The new marketing authorisation was granted on 26 November 2026 to Menarini.
More information can be found in the Summary of Product Characteristics and Patient Information leaflets which will be published on the MHRA Products website within 7 days of approval.
The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) is responsible for regulating all medicines and medical devices in the UK by ensuring they work and are acceptably safe. All our work is underpinned by robust and fact-based judgements to ensure that the benefits justify any risks.
